agent_skills.page_subtitle: Create progressive procedure packs and attach them to llm_node.
agent_skills.how_subtitle: The agent does not get every procedure at once. It sees a short index, loads a skill when needed, then unlocks tools and reference files.
agent_skills.how_step1_text: Only name and description are visible before load. Keep descriptions concrete: what the skill does and when to use it.
agent_skills.how_step2_text: Runtime injects load_agent_skill automatically when the node has attached skills. Magic tools are not listed in standing Tools.
agent_skills.how_step3_text: After load, the skill body enters context and tool_refs appear in the active tool set. depends_on children can load at depth 1.
agent_skills.field_description_hint: Shown to the agent before load (Tier-1 index).
agent_skills.field_tool_refs_hint: These tools stay hidden until the skill is loaded. Click a chip to view and edit like on llm_node.
agent_skills.field_depends_on_hint: The parent lists child skills. After load_agent_skill(parent), children are available at depth 1 (one more load). Not the same as attaching skills on llm_node.
agent_skills.field_references_hint: Tier-3 docs readable via read_agent_skill_reference after load. Click to open in the file viewer.
agent_skills.field_assets_hint: Templates and other files bound to the skill. Click to open in the file viewer.
agent_skills.delete_confirm: Delete skill "{{name}}"? Nodes that still list this id will fail on load.
agent_skills.duplicate_field_id_hint: New slug. The original skill is left unchanged.

llm_config_editor.humanitec_llms_provider_tooltip: {llmsDisplayLabel} is the platform virtual provider: it routes requests to free models from the shared verified free pool.
llm_config_editor.humanitec_llms_auto_tooltip: auto selects a free model from request requirements: tools, structured output, files/images, context, and model scoring.
llm_config_editor.provider_hint: Select the model endpoint family. For production, prefer pinning the provider through an LLM resource and keep node-level values as intentional overrides.
llm_config_editor.model_hint: The model affects quality, latency, cost, and support for tools or structured output. When unsure, use a resource or the provider auto-selection.
llm_config_editor.fallback_models_hint: Fallbacks are tried in order when the primary model call is unavailable or unsuitable. Keep the list short and compatible with tools/JSON schema.
llm_config_editor.temperature_hint: Higher values make responses more varied. For tool-calling and strict JSON, keep this low.
llm_config_editor.max_tokens_hint: Caps the model response length. Too small a value may truncate reasoning, tool calls, or JSON.
llm_config_editor.api_key_hint: Use @var:KEY to read a secret from variables. Do not paste real keys into public flows.
llm_config_editor.folder_id_hint: Yandex Cloud folder identifier for models that require it. Usually stored with provider configuration.
llm_config_editor.base_url_hint: Overrides the compatible API endpoint. Use this for self-hosted or proxy providers.
llm_config_editor.top_p_hint: Limits token choice by probability mass. Usually tune either top-p or temperature, not both at once.
llm_config_editor.top_k_hint: Limits token choice to the nearest k candidates when the provider supports it.
llm_config_editor.frequency_penalty_hint: Reduces repeated tokens. Useful for long prose, risky for strict output formats.
llm_config_editor.presence_penalty_hint: Encourages the model to introduce new topics. Operational agents usually leave this empty.
llm_config_editor.seed_hint: Fixes randomness for providers that support seed. It does not guarantee identical output after model changes.
llm_config_editor.reasoning_effort_hint: Controls reasoning depth for models that support it. More effort is usually slower and more expensive.
llm_config_editor.extra_request_body_hint: This JSON is merged into the request body last. Use it only for provider-specific parameters not represented in the form.
llm_config_editor.extra_request_headers_hint: Headers are added to the model request. Values can reference @var so secrets stay out of the flow.
llm_config_editor.extra_header_name_hint: HTTP header name, for example Authorization or X-Custom-Header.
llm_config_editor.extra_header_value_hint: String header value. Use @var:KEY for secrets.
llm_config_editor.merge_layers_hint: Extra body fields and headers are merged last and override platform defaults (including Authorization and Content-Type).

llm_context_editor.profile_hint: Ready-made behavior preset. Disabled turns the layer off; Window only keeps a short history; Memory + retrieval adds memory/RAG; Agent gives more memory and RAG budget for complex agents.
llm_context_editor.mode_hint: Main context assembly mode. off leaves messages unchanged; window keeps only the active window; smart adds memory/RAG within budgets; agent uses long-term memory more actively.
llm_context_editor.memory_hint: Where previous conversation episodes can come from. off disables memory; session uses this session; node uses this node; flow uses the whole flow; company uses company memory.
llm_context_editor.retrieval_hint: How relevant history and knowledge are searched. semantic searches by meaning; lexical by words; hybrid uses both; off disables retrieval.
llm_context_editor.budget_hint: Preset for context size. The runtime still clamps the real maximum to the selected model context length.
llm_context_editor.top_k_hint: How many memory/RAG candidates to fetch before filtering and rerank. Higher values find more, but cost more and can add noise.
llm_context_editor.min_score_hint: Minimum relevance from 0 to 1. Blocks below this threshold are not added to context.
llm_context_editor.rerank_hint: Second-pass sorting for retrieved blocks. Usually improves memory/RAG selection quality, but adds a little latency.
llm_context_editor.compaction_hint: How old messages and large blocks are compressed. auto compresses when needed; force is aggressive; off disables compaction.
llm_context_editor.cache_hint: Prompt caching hints. provider_hints enables provider-specific cache hints when the provider supports them.
llm_context_editor.max_input_tokens_hint: Hard maximum for input context before the answer. If the selected model supports less, runtime clamps this automatically.
llm_context_editor.active_window_tokens_hint: How many recent messages are kept verbatim. This is the live part of the conversation, not a summary.
llm_context_editor.memory_tokens_hint: Token budget for retrieved memory episodes.
llm_context_editor.rag_tokens_hint: Token budget for RAG documents and knowledge.
llm_context_editor.tool_result_tokens_hint: Token budget reserved for tool results before calling the LLM.
llm_context_editor.output_reserve_tokens_hint: Reserve for the model answer, so input context cannot consume the full limit.
llm_context_editor.reasoning_reserve_tokens_hint: Reserve for models that need extra reasoning budget.
llm_context_editor.safety_buffer_tokens_hint: Technical buffer for service tokens and token counting error.

llm_node_editor.prompt_help: Describe the node role, response rules, and variables. Supports {state}, @state:, and @var: references; verify preview before publishing.
llm_node_editor.llm_section_help: Choose the model and generation parameters for this node. When an LLM is pinned as a branch resource, this section becomes read-only and shows the effective config.
llm_node_editor.llm_resource_legacy_hint: One LLM resource is pinned on the node but not set as the base. Bind it to apply at runtime.
llm_node_editor.context_resource_hint: If a flow or node has exactly one llm_context resource, runtime selects it automatically; use this field only to disambiguate.
llm_node_editor.context_section_help: Context controls memory, retrieval, and message window. Override it on the node only when this node needs a different memory profile.
llm_node_editor.messages_filter_help: The filter limits which previous node messages enter the current prompt. Use custom when this node should see only selected results.
llm_node_editor.output_mode_hint: Tools: the assistant may call tools and respond in natural language. Structured: the reply is a JSON object validated against the output schema below.
llm_node_editor.output_mode_help: Tools mode is for actions and ReAct. Structured output is for cases where the next node expects strict JSON and no tool calls.
llm_node_editor.output_schema_strict_hint: For strict JSON Schema use a root object: every key in properties must appear in required; on each object that defines properties set additionalProperties: false.
llm_node_editor.output_schema_help: The schema validates the model's final JSON. Precise fields and descriptions make downstream state handling easier.
llm_node_editor.react_section_help: ReAct enables multiple thought -> tool -> observation steps. Cap iterations and define exit policy so the flow cannot loop forever.
llm_node_editor.tools_section_help: The tools list defines which actions the LLM node may call. Add only necessary tools to reduce noise and wrong calls.
llm_node_editor.flow_tool_call_type_aria: Toggle the call mode for sub-agent {{name}}
llm_node_editor.flow_tool_call_type_hint: Call returns a result to the current run; Handoff transfers the following dialog to the child flow.
llm_node_editor.react_loop_mode_hint: auto ends based on the model response. explicit requires an exit tool call and is better for controlled workflows.
llm_node_editor.react_max_iterations_hint: Hard cap on ReAct steps in one run. 10-25 is usually enough; higher values increase cost and latency.
llm_node_editor.react_strict: Strict mode (reminder when exit_tool not used)
llm_node_editor.react_exit_tool_hint: Tool used by the model to end an explicit loop. The name must match the sanitized tool name visible to the LLM.
llm_node_editor.react_reminder_hint: Added when the model did not finish an explicit loop. Keep it short and tell the model how to call the exit tool.
llm_node_editor.agent_skills_section_help: The agent sees skill names and descriptions in the prompt. Full procedures and tools unlock only after load_agent_skill. Meta-tools (load_agent_skill, read_agent_skill_reference) are injected automatically on attach and never appear in standing Tools chips.

reflection_node_editor.intro_body: An LLM critic checks the selected state slice against criteria and writes the verdict to state.validation (including exit_id). Named exits live in the policy — canvas ports use their labels; edges get validation.exit_id == <exit_id> conditions.
reflection_node_editor.section_exits_hint: Order is first-match after the gate. You can put when=always last as a catch-all. Every exit_id must have an outgoing edge.
reflection_node_editor.section_llm_hint: Model is only used for the critic verdict. Tools and fallbacks are not allowed on reflection.
reflection_node_editor.preset_final_answer_subtitle: Check text before sending it to the user
reflection_node_editor.preset_transaction_subtitle: Safety of side effects before execution
reflection_node_editor.preset_quality_subtitle: Completeness and accuracy of the output
reflection_node_editor.policy_id_hint: Label for logs and state.validation.policy_id — not a catalog reference
reflection_node_editor.gate_hint: Label in the result and traces. Blocking rules are the same for every type.
reflection_node_editor.instruction_hint: Prompt text for the critic model, not for the chat user
reflection_node_editor.min_confidence_hint: If confidence is below this threshold — gate is not approved
reflection_node_editor.block_on_severities_hint: If the critic finds an issue with this severity — gate is not approved

when_descriptions.blocked_reason_prefix: Matches if any blocked_reason starts with the prefix
when_descriptions.always: Catches everything left; must be last in the list

gate_descriptions.final_answer: Check text before delivering it to the user
gate_descriptions.transaction: Check an action / side effect before execution

severity_descriptions.critical: Unsafe side effect or hard ban

remote_flow_editor.protocol_lead: The remote side must be a compatible A2A agent. Older protocols (0.3 and below) are not supported.
remote_flow_editor.protocol_bullet_version: HTTP header A2A-Version: 1.0 on every request
remote_flow_editor.protocol_bullet_skills: Agent capabilities live in Agent Card skills[] (id / name / description)
remote_flow_editor.protocol_bullet_metadata: SendMessage can carry params.metadata (JSON); on the platform, metadata.variables merge into flow variables
remote_flow_editor.url_hint: Base A2A agent endpoint (no trailing slash). Example: https://host/flows/api/v1/my-flow
remote_flow_editor.skill_hint: id from Agent Card skills[]. For a platform flow this is the remote graph branch_id. Empty or default — primary skill. Third-party agents may ignore the selection.
remote_flow_editor.metadata_hint: Root JSON object → params.metadata. In strings: whole @state:path or @var:path; or @var: embeds in text. For a platform agent use the variables key. The branch key is controlled by Skill ID above.

base_resource_editor.permission_hint: Empty list — available to all flow participants. Otherwise the user needs membership in one of these OpenFGA groups.

rag_resource_editor.what_is_hint: Flow knowledge base: documents live in a Namespace; llm_node pulls fragments into context. Explicit search/write uses rag_search / rag_add_text.
rag_resource_editor.hint_namespace: Company knowledge space name. Same value is namespace_id in the RAG API and tools.
rag_resource_editor.hint_namespace_create: Latin letters, digits, _ and -. Example: kb-support. After create it is bound to this resource.
rag_resource_editor.hint_namespace_description: Human-readable purpose. Needed when creating a new namespace; leave empty if it already exists.
rag_resource_editor.namespace_description_placeholder: e.g. Support FAQ and return policies
rag_resource_editor.namespace_name_invalid: Name: latin letters, digits, _ and -; starts with a letter; up to 64 characters.
rag_resource_editor.hint_default_top_k: How many text chunks from the base go into context / search results. Typical range: 3–8.
rag_resource_editor.hint_collection_id: Optional tag inside the namespace: search and write only documents with this collection_id. Empty = whole namespace.
rag_resource_editor.index_hint: Optional: how documents are split on upload. Empty fields = platform defaults. Embedding model is not set here.
rag_resource_editor.hint_chunk_size: Approx. fragment size in tokens. Larger = wider chunk context, less precision.
rag_resource_editor.hint_chunk_overlap: Tokens repeated between neighboring chunks so meaning is not lost at boundaries.
rag_resource_editor.hint_default_ttl: After how many seconds background cleanup removes this resource’s documents. 0 = keep forever. Empty = platform default.
rag_resource_editor.documents_disabled: Pick a namespace first — then you can upload files into the index.
rag_resource_editor.documents_drop: Drop a file here or use the paperclip

api_console.title: API and A2A
api_console.hero_title: Call this flow through the API
api_console.hero_subtitle: This flow is called through A2A JSON-RPC. Switch the mode below: the UI will update method, Accept header, metadata, and examples for the current flow.
api_console.mode_stream_text: method SendStreamingMessage, Accept text/event-stream, header A2A-Version: 1.0. The client reads SSE frames and receives the answer in chunks.
api_console.mode_sync_text: method SendMessage, Accept application/json, header A2A-Version: 1.0. The HTTP request waits for the flow to finish and returns the final A2A Task.
api_console.mode_async_text: method SendMessage with configuration.returnImmediately=true. The response is TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED immediately; fetch the result through GetTask.
api_console.modes_text: A2A uses one flow endpoint, with different methods and response expectations. This selector updates both live-run and code examples.
api_console.quick_step_1_text: POST /flows/api/v1/{flow_id}. GET on the same URL returns the Agent Card; the well-known URL sits next to it.
api_console.quick_step_2_text: messageId is unique for the message, role is ROLE_USER, parts contains {text} or {raw|url}, contextId fixes the conversation.
api_console.quick_step_3_text: Streaming reads SSE, sync waits for the final Task, async returns TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED and is polled with GetTask.
api_console.method_stream: Main chat mode. Returns an SSE stream and emits the answer in chunks.
api_console.method_send: Synchronous call. If configuration.returnImmediately=true, returns a submitted task without waiting for the final result.
api_console.method_get: Get a Task by task_id or contextId. historyLength limits history.
api_console.method_cancel: Cancel execution. id can be task_id or contextId.
api_console.method_subscribe_to_task: SubscribeToTask: live tail after pause (snapshot + Redis events).
api_console.method_card: GetExtendedAgentCard when configured; otherwise JSON-RPC error (no silent fallback).
api_console.auth_text: From the browser, this console uses the current cookie session. External clients usually send Authorization: Bearer <token>. Host/subdomain selects the company context.
api_console.instruction_title: Open the full API Console guide
api_console.file_example_text: A file is sent as Part.url or Part.raw (filename, mediaType). External Part.url is fetched server-side with SSRF guard into state.files. Audio also goes through STT.
api_console.field_jsonrpc: Always "2.0". This is the JSON-RPC envelope version.
api_console.field_id: String or integer. Echoed in every frame so the client can match response to request.
api_console.field_method: A2A Protocol 1.0 method. Streaming uses SendStreamingMessage; sync and async use SendMessage.
api_console.field_params: Method params. For SendMessage/SendStreamingMessage this contains message and metadata.
api_console.field_message_id: Unique client-side message id. It is not task_id.
api_console.field_role: Message author role. For external requests this is ROLE_USER.
api_console.field_parts: Array of parts without kind: {text}, {raw,filename?,mediaType?}, {url,filename?,mediaType?}, or {data,mediaType?}.
api_console.field_context_id: Conversation id. The same contextId resumes the runtime session; backend stores it as flow_id:context_id.
api_console.field_task_id: Optional. Usually omitted; backend creates task_id and returns it through SSE.
api_console.field_metadata: Run options: branch, variables, version, breakpoints, triggers.
api_console.field_branch: Selects the graph branch. UI base maps to default. metadata.variables.branch_id does not select the branch.
api_console.field_variables: Runtime variables for this run. @var:key strings resolve through VariablesService, including nested JSON and recursive references. variables.branch_id does not select the graph branch, but is copied to target_branch_id when target_branch_id is not provided.
api_console.field_version: Optional flow config version. Query ?v=... takes precedence over metadata.version.
api_console.field_breakpoints: Debug-only: object {node_id: true}. Used by the editor to stop on nodes.
api_console.field_triggers: Advanced: trigger runtime context snapshot. Normal API clients do not need it.
api_console.field_return_immediately: A2A 1.0 configuration.returnImmediately: true returns a TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED Task without waiting; false/omit blocks until terminal/interrupted.
api_console.variables_text: Flow variables override company variables. @var supports only @var:key and @var:nested.path; missing keys fail the run, with no empty defaults.
api_console.var_field_value: JSON variable value. Can be @var:company_secret, resolved before the run.
api_console.var_field_secret: Masks the value in UI. Runtime behavior depends only on value.
api_console.var_field_public: Shows the variable in the Agent Card as a parameter external developers should fill.
api_console.var_field_description: Explains what to put into the variable and in what format.
api_console.current_variables_empty: This branch has no flow variables yet.
api_console.system_variables_text: Backend adds these after metadata.variables and prevents clients from spoofing user or company identity.
api_console.live_text: The run uses the same A2A endpoint from the current browser session. Examples on the left update from these same fields.
api_console.run_text: Click Run to send SendStreamingMessage and receive the real flow response.
api_console.run_text_stream: Run sends SendStreamingMessage and shows the answer collected from real SSE frames.
api_console.run_text_sync: Run sends SendMessage and waits for the final A2A Task in the JSON-RPC response.
api_console.run_text_async: Run sends SendMessage with configuration.returnImmediately=true. The response is TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED; use task_id/contextId with GetTask.
api_console.result_empty: The response will appear after a run.
api_console.result_no_text: No text response was found. Inspect the full JSON/SSE payload below.
api_console.default_message: Hi! Reply in one short sentence.

hints.templates: Templates create a ready case in the selected suite. They cover deterministic checks, built-in metrics, trace assertions, code checks, LLM judge, and multi-turn scenarios.
hints.run_scope: Suite runs every enabled case. Case runs only the selected case. Trials repeat each case to expose nondeterminism.
hints.run_options: Trials is the number of repeats for each case. Parallel is max case-run concurrency inside the durable TaskIQ job.
hints.case_editor: A case has turns (input + check), optional tags, and a strict typed check. Input: text, inline_code, or a flow llm_node. LLM judge references a rubric version and judge_node_id in FlowConfig.
hints.case_name: A short name that helps developers find the regression or smoke case in the matrix.
hints.case_tags: Comma-separated tags: smoke, regression, safety, tool-use. They help filter suites and analyze results.
hints.case_description: Describe which flow behavior this test case protects and why failure matters.
hints.case_input: Turn input: user text, an inline_code generator, or a flow llm_node (tester). For node input the case stores only node_id.
hints.tester_node: Pick a flow llm_node that generates the user message once per turn. The harness drives the case turn list — the tester does not decide when the test ends. Create writes an orphan node into FlowConfig.
hints.judge_node: Judge is an llm_node in FlowConfig. The case stores only judge_node_id; edit the judge as a flow node.
hints.rubric: Versioned Evaluation Lab rubric (criteria + pass_threshold). Do not merge it with the judge node.
hints.check_type: Choose one scorer: deterministic, trace, built-in metric, LLM judge, or isolated code. Every type maps to the backend union contract.
hints.contains_values: The case passes when the response contains at least one expected fragment.
hints.not_contains_values: The case passes when the response excludes blocked phrases, errors, or unsafe content.
hints.regex_pattern: Regular expression for strict formats: order number, JSON fragment, date, or email.
hints.min_chars: Minimum response length. Leave empty if only an upper bound is needed.
hints.max_chars: Maximum response length. Leave empty if only a lower bound is needed.
hints.state_path: Path inside the state snapshot, for example response, structured_output.answer, or tool_result.status.
hints.state_operator: Operator: exists, eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte.
hints.trace_value: Node ID, tool node ID, or tool_call_id expected in trace/workflow history.
hints.rubric_version_id: Rubric version for LLM judge. Backend requires a structured tool-call result, not free JSON in text.
hints.metric_id: Built-in evaluator ID from the catalog: ROUGE-L, BLEU, toxicity, safety, groundedness, answer relevance, tool accuracy.
hints.reference: Reference answer or grounding context for metrics that require it.
hints.sidebar_suites: A suite is a dataset/test suite for a flow. It contains cases that run as experiments/runs.
hints.sidebar_cases: A case is one scenario under test. Select it to edit input/check or run only that case.
hints.sidebar_workspace: Workspace switches the right panel: editor, compare, trace, and monitoring. The matrix and transcript stay visible.
hints.sidebar_evaluators: The catalog shows available scorers: deterministic, safety, retrieval, trace, and pairwise.
hints.matrix: The matrix shows runs x cases. Click a run to select an experiment, or a cell to open its case-run, transcript, and trace.
hints.transcript: Transcript shows the live case-run dialog and append-only events: case_started, message, score_recorded, case_finished.
hints.compare: Compare evaluates baseline/current runs, sets a branch baseline, and records human or LLM pairwise judgments.
hints.trace: Trace links the case-run result to spans, tool calls, workflow records, and state history.
hints.monitoring: This panel shows CI/nightly gates, baselines, and online monitors for production traces.

templates.menu_subtitle: Templates cover every main eval-case and scorer type.
templates.contains_description: Checks that the response contains an expected fragment.
templates.not_contains_description: Blocks unsafe/error phrases in the response.
templates.regex_description: Checks a strict response format with a regular expression.
templates.length_description: Controls minimum and maximum response length.
templates.state_path_description: Checks a value or presence inside the state snapshot.
templates.json_schema_description: Validates structured output with JSON Schema.
templates.trace_tool_description: Checks that the expected tool/node was actually called.

case_editor.tester_node_default_prompt:
You are the user in Evaluation Lab: simulate a real person chatting with the flow under test.

How the run works (important):
- A case has a fixed list of turns. The harness calls you exactly once per turn.
- You receive the dialog so far (USER/ASSISTANT).
- You do NOT decide when the test ends: turn count and checks belong to the case, not to you.
- After your message the flow replies, then that turn's checks run (contains, judge, etc.).

How to behave:
- Reply with only the next user message — no preamble, quotes, "User:", markdown wrappers, or commentary.
- Sound like a natural product user: concise, clear intent.
- One goal per turn (clarify, request an action, complain, confirm).
- Use the assistant's last reply: do not repeat yourself; advance the dialog.
- If asked for data, invent plausible details (name, date, order id) without breaking character.
- Stay in role: you are not a judge or engineer; do not critique answer quality.

Good example:
"Please start a refund for order 45821 — the package never arrived."

Bad example:
"As a user I want to test refunds. Generate a request."
case_editor.judge_node_default_prompt:
You are a strict LLM judge in Evaluation Lab.

Contract (required):
- Score the assistant reply strictly against the case rubric.
- Call the `record_evaluation_judgment` tool exactly once.
- Tool args: scores (object), total_score (0..10 or null), passed (boolean), feedback (string or null).
- Do not write free-form text/JSON instead of the tool call — the harness accepts only the tool invocation.
- Be consistent: similar replies → similar scores.
- Keep feedback brief with concrete pass/fail reasons.
